message.content:
This is a gasket of polyurethane plastic foam, a part for aviation headsets. Candidate headings:

- 3926.90 covers other articles of plastics. Cellular plastics fall under chapter 39, and an article made of plastic foam would be classified in 3926.90.99 unless a more specific provision applies.
- 8547 or 8518.90 would cover parts of headsets. Heading 8518 includes headphones and earphones, and 8518.90 covers their parts. But Section XVI Note 1(b) excludes parts of general use, and Note 2(b) covers parts suitable for use solely with a machine. A foam gasket that is a part of a headset could arguably fall in 8518.90. Heading 3926 is not excluded by Section XVI notes, though, because Note 1(c) in Section XVI excludes only certain items (e.g., Chapter 39 articles are not named?). In fact Section XVI Note 1(a) excludes articles of plastics of Chapter 39 only for transmission belts. Actually, Note 1(a) excludes transmission or conveyor belts of plastics, and Note 1(b) excludes certain other items, so a foam gasket is not categorically excluded from 8518.90.
- CBP rulings on foam microphone windscreens or gaskets for headsets have generally classified them as parts of headsets under 8518.90.80 when dedicated. However, a plain foam gasket is more likely to be classified as an article of plastics.

I chose 3926.90.9990 (other articles of plastics, other), because the gasket is a simple foam article, and I did not confirm that it is a dedicated headset part.
